   177→    def contains(self, version: Version, resolve_prerelease: Optional[bool]):
   178→        """
   179→        Whether <version> is inside the version range
   180→
   181→        :param version: Version to check against
   182→        :param resolve_prerelease: If ``True``, ensure prereleases can be resolved in this range
   183→        If ``False``, prerelases can NOT be resolved in this range
   184→        If ``None``, prereleases are resolved only if this version range expression says so
   185→        :return: Whether the version is inside the range
   186→        """
   187→        assert isinstance(version, Version), type(version)
   188→        for condition_set in self.condition_sets:
   189→            if condition_set.valid(version, resolve_prerelease):
   190→                return True
   191→        return False

   193→    def intersection(self, other):
   194→        conditions = []
   195→
   196→        def _calculate_limits(operator, lhs, rhs):
   197→            limits = ([c for c in lhs.conditions if operator in c.operator]
   198→                      + [c for c in rhs.conditions if operator in c.operator])
   199→            if limits:
   200→                return sorted(limits, reverse=operator == ">")[0]
   201→
   202→        prerelease = True
   203→        for lhs_conditions in self.condition_sets:
   204→            for rhs_conditions in other.condition_sets:
   205→                internal_conditions = []
   206→                lower_limit = _calculate_limits(">", lhs_conditions, rhs_conditions)
   207→                upper_limit = _calculate_limits("<", lhs_conditions, rhs_conditions)
   208→                if lower_limit:
   209→                    internal_conditions.append(lower_limit)
   210→                if upper_limit:
   211→                    internal_conditions.append(upper_limit)
   212→                if internal_conditions and (not lower_limit or not upper_limit or lower_limit <= upper_limit):
   213→                    conditions.append(internal_conditions)
   214→                # conservative approach: if any of the conditions forbid prereleases, forbid them in the result
   215→                if not lhs_conditions.prerelease or not rhs_conditions.prerelease:
   216→                    prerelease = False
   217→
   218→        if not conditions:
   219→            return None
   220→        expression = ' || '.join(' '.join(str(c) for c in cs) for cs in conditions) + (', include_prerelease' if prerelease else '')
   221→        result = VersionRange(expression)
   222→        # TODO: Direct definition of conditions not reparsing
   223→        # result.condition_sets = self.condition_sets + other.condition_sets
   224→        return result

   224→        propagating includes or libs or run info or both are visible or the reference is the same,
   225→        we consider the requires equal, so they can conflict"""

   228→                 (self.headers and other.headers) or
   229→                 (self.libs and other.libs) or

   234→    def aggregate(self, other):
   235→        """ when closing loop and finding the same dependency on a node, the information needs
   236→        to be aggregated
   237→        :param other: is the existing Require that the current node has, which information has to be
   238→        appended to "self", which is the requires that is being propagated to the current node
   239→        from upstream
   240→        """
   241→        assert self.build == other.build
   242→        if other.override:
   243→            # If the other aggregated is an override, it shouldn't add information
   244→            # it already did override upstream, and the actual information used in this node is
   245→            # the propagated one.
   246→            self.force = True
   247→            return
   248→        self.headers |= other.headers
   249→        self.libs |= other.libs
   250→        self.run = self.run or other.run
   251→        self.visible |= other.visible
   252→        self.force |= other.force
   253→        self.direct |= other.direct
   254→        self.transitive_headers = self.transitive_headers or other.transitive_headers
   255→        self.transitive_libs = self.transitive_libs or other.transitive_libs
   256→        if not other.test:
   257→            self.test = False  # it it was previously a test, but also required by non-test
   258→        self.is_test = self.is_test or other.is_test
   259→        # package_id_mode is not being propagated downstream. So it is enough to check if the
   260→        # current require already defined it or not
   261→        if self.package_id_mode is None:
   262→            self.package_id_mode = other.package_id_mode
   263→        self.required_nodes.extend(other.required_nodes)

   265→    def transform_downstream(self, pkg_type, require, dep_pkg_type):
   266→        """
   267→        consumer ---self--->  foo<pkg_type> ---require---> bar<dep_pkg_type>
   268→            \\ -------------------????-------------------- /
   269→        Compute new Requirement to be applied to "consumer" translating the effect of the dependency
   270→        to such "consumer".
   271→        Result can be None if nothing is to be propagated
   272→        """
   273→        if require.visible is False:
   274→            # TODO: We could implement checks in case private is violated (e.g shared libs)
   275→            return
   276→
   277→        if require.build:  # public!
   278→            # TODO: To discuss if this way of conflicting build_requires is actually useful or not
   279→            # Build-requires will propagate its main trait for running exes/shared to downstream
   280→            # consumers so run=require.run, irrespective of the 'self.run' trait
   281→            downstream_require = Requirement(require.ref, headers=False, libs=False, build=True,
   282→                                             run=require.run, visible=self.visible, direct=False)
   283→            return downstream_require
   284→
   285→        if self.build:  # Build-requires
   286→            # If the above is shared or the requirement is explicit run=True
   287→            # visible=self.visible will further propagate it downstream
   288→            if dep_pkg_type is PackageType.SHARED or require.run:
   289→                downstream_require = Requirement(require.ref, headers=False, libs=False, build=True,
   290→                                                 run=True, visible=self.visible, direct=False)
   291→                return downstream_require
   292→            return
   293→
   294→        # Regular and test requires
   295→        if dep_pkg_type is PackageType.SHARED or dep_pkg_type is PackageType.STATIC:
   296→            if pkg_type is PackageType.SHARED:
   297→                downstream_require = Requirement(require.ref, headers=False, libs=False, run=require.run)
   298→            elif pkg_type is PackageType.STATIC:
   299→                downstream_require = Requirement(require.ref, headers=False, libs=require.libs, run=require.run)
   300→            elif pkg_type is PackageType.APP:
   301→                downstream_require = Requirement(require.ref, headers=False, libs=False, run=require.run)
   302→            elif pkg_type is PackageType.HEADER:
   303→                downstream_require = Requirement(require.ref, headers=require.headers, libs=require.libs, run=require.run)
   304→            else:
   305→                assert pkg_type == PackageType.UNKNOWN
   306→                # TODO: This is undertested, changing it did not break tests
   307→                downstream_require = require.copy_requirement()
   308→        elif dep_pkg_type is PackageType.HEADER:
   309→            downstream_require = Requirement(require.ref, headers=False, libs=False, run=require.run)
   310→        else:
   311→            # Unknown, default. This happens all the time while check_downstream as shared is unknown
   312→            # FIXME
   313→            downstream_require = require.copy_requirement()
   314→            # This is faster than pkg_type in (pkg.shared, pkg.static, ....)
   315→            if pkg_type is PackageType.SHARED or pkg_type is PackageType.APP:
   316→                downstream_require.libs = False
   317→                downstream_require.headers = False
   318→            elif pkg_type is PackageType.STATIC:
   319→                downstream_require.headers = False
   320→
   321→        assert require.visible, "at this point require should be visible"
   322→
   323→        if require.transitive_headers is not None:
   324→            downstream_require.headers = require.headers and require.transitive_headers
   325→        if self.transitive_headers is not None:
   326→            downstream_require.transitive_headers = self.transitive_headers
   327→
   328→        if require.transitive_libs is not None:
   329→            downstream_require.libs = require.libs and require.transitive_libs
   330→        if self.transitive_libs is not None:
   331→            downstream_require.transitive_libs = self.transitive_libs
   332→
   333→        if self.visible is False:
   334→            downstream_require.visible = False
   335→
   336→        if pkg_type is not PackageType.HEADER:  # These rules are not valid for header-only
   337→            # If non-default, then the consumer requires has priority
   338→            if self.headers is False:
   339→                downstream_require.headers = False
   340→
   341→            if self.libs is False:
   342→                downstream_require.libs = False
   343→
   344→        # TODO: Automatic assignment invalidates user possibility of overriding default
   345→        # if required.run is not None:
   346→        #    downstream_require.run = required.run
   347→
   348→        if self.test:
   349→            downstream_require.test = True
   350→        downstream_require.is_test = require.is_test
   351→
   352→        # If the current one is resolving conflicts, the downstream one will be too
   353→        downstream_require.force = require.force
   354→        downstream_require.direct = False
   355→        return downstream_require

   357→    def deduce_package_id_mode(self, pkg_type, dep_node, non_embed_mode, embed_mode, build_mode,
   358→                               unknown_mode):
   359→        # If defined by the ``require(package_id_mode=xxx)`` trait, that is higher priority
   360→        # The "conf" values are defaults, no hard overrides
   361→        if self.package_id_mode:
   362→            return
   363→
   364→        if self.test:
   365→            return  # test_requires never affect the binary_id
   366→        dep_conanfile = dep_node.conanfile
   367→        dep_pkg_type = dep_conanfile.package_type
   368→        if self.build:
   369→            build_mode = getattr(dep_conanfile, "build_mode", build_mode)
   370→            if build_mode and self.direct:
   371→                self.package_id_mode = build_mode
   372→            return
   373→
   374→        if pkg_type is PackageType.HEADER:
   375→            self.package_id_mode = "unrelated_mode"
   376→            return
   377→
   378→        # If the dependency defines the mode, that has priority over default
   379→        embed_mode = getattr(dep_conanfile, "package_id_embed_mode", embed_mode)
   380→        non_embed_mode = getattr(dep_conanfile, "package_id_non_embed_mode", non_embed_mode)
   381→        unknown_mode = getattr(dep_conanfile, "package_id_unknown_mode", unknown_mode)
   382→        if self.headers or self.libs:  # only if linked
   383→            if pkg_type is PackageType.SHARED or pkg_type is PackageType.APP:
   384→                if dep_pkg_type is PackageType.SHARED:
   385→                    self.package_id_mode = non_embed_mode
   386→                else:
   387→                    self.package_id_mode = embed_mode
   388→            elif pkg_type is PackageType.STATIC:
   389→                if dep_pkg_type is PackageType.HEADER:
   390→                    self.package_id_mode = embed_mode
   391→                else:
   392→                    self.package_id_mode = non_embed_mode
   393→
   394→            if self.package_id_mode is None:
   395→                self.package_id_mode = unknown_mode

   546→    def _run_cli(self, command_line, assert_error=False):
   547→        current_dir = os.getcwd()
   548→        os.chdir(self.current_folder)
   549→        old_path = sys.path[:]
   550→        old_modules = list(sys.modules.keys())
   551→
   552→        args = shlex.split(command_line)
   553→
   554→        try:
   555→            self.api = ConanAPI(cache_folder=self.cache_folder)
   556→            command = Cli(self.api)
   557→        except ConanException as e:
   558→            sys.stderr.write("Error in Conan initialization: {}".format(e))
   559→            return ERROR_GENERAL
   560→
   561→        error = SUCCESS
   562→        trace = None
   563→        try:
   564→            if self._custom_commands_folder:
   565→                with environment_update({_CONAN_INTERNAL_CUSTOM_COMMANDS_PATH:
   566→                                             self._custom_commands_folder}):
   567→                    command.run(args)
   568→            else:
   569→                command.run(args)
   570→        except BaseException as e:  # Capture all exceptions as argparse
   571→            trace = traceback.format_exc()
   572→            error = command.exception_exit_error(e)
   573→        finally:
   574→            sys.path = old_path
   575→            os.chdir(current_dir)
   576→            # Reset sys.modules to its prev state. A .copy() DOES NOT WORK
   577→            added_modules = set(sys.modules).difference(old_modules)
   578→            for added in added_modules:
   579→                sys.modules.pop(added, None)
   580→        self._handle_cli_result(command_line, assert_error=assert_error, error=error, trace=trace)
   581→        return error

   583→    def run(self, command_line, assert_error=False, redirect_stdout=None, redirect_stderr=None, inputs=None):
   584→        """ run a single command as in the command line.
   585→            If user or password is filled, user_io will be mocked to return this
   586→            tuple if required
   587→        """
   588→        from conan.test.utils.mocks import RedirectedTestOutput
   589→        with environment_update({"NO_COLOR": "1"}):  # Not initialize colorama in testing
   590→            self.user_inputs = RedirectedInputStream(inputs or self.inputs)
   591→            self.stdout = RedirectedTestOutput()  # Initialize each command
   592→            self.stderr = RedirectedTestOutput()
   593→            self.out = ""
   594→            with self.mocked_io():
   595→                real_servers = any(isinstance(s, (str, ArtifactoryServer))
   596→                                   for s in self.servers.values())
   597→                http_requester = None
   598→                if not real_servers:
   599→                    if self.requester_class:
   600→                        http_requester = self.requester_class(self.servers)
   601→                    else:
   602→                        http_requester = TestRequester(self.servers)
   603→                try:

   605→                        with self.mocked_servers(http_requester):
   606→                            return self._run_cli(command_line, assert_error=assert_error)
   607→                    else:
   608→                        return self._run_cli(command_line, assert_error=assert_error)
   609→                finally:
   610→                    self.stdout = str(self.stdout)
   611→                    self.stderr = str(self.stderr)
   612→                    self.out = self.stderr + self.stdout
   613→                    if redirect_stdout:

   640→                header='{:=^80}'.format(msg),
   641→                output_header='{:=^80}'.format(" Output: "),
   642→                cmd=command,
   643→                output=str(self.stderr) + str(self.stdout) + "\n" + str(self.out)

   645→            if trace:
   646→                exc_message += '{:=^80}'.format(" Traceback: ") + f"\n{trace}"
